title: The Memorial Account Closes and Sirhind's Hidden Wealth Reappears

blocks.text: This page closes the memorial episode by stressing the purpose of written preservation. The account is said to have been set down so the Khalsa could hear, read and pray at the shrine, giving the memorial both literary and devotional continuity.

From there the poem pivots into a new Sirhind-centered episode focused on remaining forts, buried treasure, and unfinished seizure. The city has already been judged and damaged, yet the search for what lies hidden beneath its structures shows that conquest is not materially complete.
The result is another hinge in the broader sequence. A site of memory remains behind, while the narrative moves back toward possession, excavation, and the struggle over what Sirhind still contains.
